description: Catalogue of the datasets shown on UK Public Money Monitor: source, refresh, basis, verification and known limitations. 'stamp' names the field in the data file that records the last refresh.

datasets.publisher: Cabinet Office (Contracts Finder, Find a Tender)
datasets.refresh: Daily at 05:20 UTC; historical backfill every 4 hours until complete
datasets.basis: Tender estimates, award values and contract values; never payments
datasets.limitations: Below-threshold and devolved-portal notices are only partly covered; the two portals overlap; framework agreement values are ceilings; suppliers are linked only by published identifiers.
Recent months are provisional. Local taxes (Council Tax, Business Rates) and devolved taxes are not HMRC receipts.

datasets.publisher: HM Revenue & Customs annual report and accounts
datasets.limitations: Transcribed from the annual report PDFs; due for an item-by-item check against the accounts.

datasets.refresh: Checked daily; Treasury publishes three times a year
datasets.unit: GBP billion (nominal and real terms) and % of GDP
datasets.basis: Total expenditure on services (outturn and plans)
datasets.limitations: TES differs from Total Managed Expenditure; plans are not outturn.

datasets.module: Public spending by country and region
datasets.unit: GBP million and GBP per person
datasets.limitations: Non-identifiable spending (e.g. most defence, debt interest) is not allocated to regions.

datasets.refresh: Checked daily; DWP publishes after each Budget and Spring Statement
datasets.unit: GBP million (nominal or real terms as labelled); caseloads in thousands
datasets.basis: Outturn, with DWP forecasts flagged separately
datasets.limitations: Great Britain only: Northern Ireland social security is paid by the NI Executive. Benefits devolved to Scotland leave these tables once transferred. Tax credits and Child Benefit (HMRC) are not DWP benefits. Every year's benefit lines are checked to add up to the published total.

datasets.refresh: Checked daily; NHS England publishes once a year. Its web page refuses automated requests, so links to a new year's files are added to data/nhs/tac-sources.json when published
datasets.basis: Audited annual accounts (income, expenses, surplus or deficit)
datasets.limitations: England only; NHS trusts and foundation trusts, not ICBs or NHS England itself. Group basis and before consolidation adjustments, so trusts cannot be added together into an NHS total. Every trust is checked for operating income minus expenses = operating result.

datasets.module: NHS Wales spending by health condition
datasets.basis: Programme budgets (NHS expenditure analysed by condition)
datasets.limitations: Wales only; local health boards and Public Health Wales. Health boards were reorganised in 2019, so their series break. Every year is checked: conditions add up to the total and broken-down conditions add up to their parts.

datasets.module: NHS Scotland payments to GP practices
datasets.publisher: Public Health Scotland and NSS Practitioner Services
datasets.limitations: Scotland only; latest six years. Payments cover practice staff, premises and running costs, not GP earnings. Dispensing doctor payments are separate. Practices are matched to names by their official practice code; every practice is checked for payment types adding up to its total.

datasets.refresh: Checked daily; published once a year
datasets.basis: Grant spending in the year (departments, schemes); award values for individual awards
datasets.limitations: UK government departments only, not devolved governments. Award amounts can cover several years. Recipients are grouped only by published identifiers; those under £100,000 are counted in totals but not listed.

datasets.module: Civil Service pay and staff by department
datasets.refresh: Checked daily; published annually (as at 31 March)
datasets.basis: Salary rates and staff numbers at a date (not pay bills)
datasets.limitations: Civil servants only (not armed forces, NHS, teachers, police or local government). Salaries exclude overtime, bonuses and pensions. Headcounts are rounded to five and small cells are suppressed. Checked: grades never exceed their total, and departments add up to the Civil Service total.

datasets.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
datasets.refresh: Checked daily; MHCLG publishes annually in March
datasets.basis: Area council tax for two adults by band, excluding parish precepts
datasets.limitations: England only; bills before discounts and support; historical years not yet loaded.

datasets.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
datasets.refresh: Checked daily; MHCLG publishes outturn annually
datasets.limitations: England only; latest five years. Councils that missed the deadline have no figures for that year. Capital spending is not included. Every row is checked for net cost = spending − income.

datasets.refresh: Checked daily; the Welsh Government publishes outturn annually (October)
datasets.limitations: From 2001-02. Service lines follow the Welsh return and are not directly comparable with England. Capital spending is not included. Every authority and year is checked: the services add up to the published revenue expenditure total.
Central-government current receipts and expenditure are not total public spending and do not give the deficit.

datasets.publisher: National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority (NISTA)
datasets.refresh: Weekly verification against the official CSV
datasets.basis: Published estimates: whole-life cost, annual baseline and forecast, benefits
datasets.limitations: Estimates, not actual spending. Some figures are exempt from publication; these are shown as not published.

datasets.publisher: IPA / NISTA annual reports (via the ProjectLens mirror)
datasets.unit: GBP, price base varies by year
datasets.limitations: Taken from a third-party mirror of the official files; price bases differ between years, so no cost-change percentages are calculated.

datasets.refresh: Weekly check for a new annual release
datasets.limitations: ODA includes in-donor refugee costs and core multilateral contributions; it is not all money sent abroad. Military aid is not ODA.

gaps.status: not yet published on this site
gaps.reason: No official machine-readable series of UK military aid exists. The Ministry of Defence publishes the net additional cost of operations by operation (Defence departmental resources, worksheet 6), but the operation names in the published spreadsheet are not machine-readable, so the figures cannot yet be attributed automatically. Pledges and announcements are not spending and are not shown.

gaps.module: Council spending in Scotland and Northern Ireland
gaps.status: not yet published on this site
gaps.reason: England and Wales are live. The Scottish Government publishes council spending in its Local Financial Returns workbooks, but gov.scot refuses automated downloads (it answers with an empty challenge page), so the figures cannot be refreshed and verified automatically. Northern Ireland's councils provide a narrower set of services and no consolidated, machine-readable outturn series by council has been found.

gaps.module: NHS commissioners in England, and the wider NHS in Scotland and Northern Ireland
gaps.reason: English NHS trust accounts, NHS Wales spending by condition and NHS Scotland payments to GP practices are live, and health spending by nation is under Regions. Integrated care board accounts are published as one PDF per board; NHS England's own pages refuse automated requests, and the Scottish Government's site does too, so these cannot yet be refreshed automatically. Northern Ireland's health trust accounts are published as PDF reports only.

gaps.module: Government property, and pay outside the Civil Service
gaps.reason: Civil Service pay and staff numbers by department are live, and grants are too. The government property estate is published as an annual report and as property records that are not yet machine-readable with values, and pay for the wider public sector (NHS, schools, armed forces, police) comes from separate pay review body and workforce statistics that are being assessed.
